sourceRules.source: supplied Set Planner app.f9354b027b.js emoteSet/emoteStep state13

measurement.scope: 214 dancing capture frames; brown arm silhouette outside the independently aligned static torso/head, excluding eyes, feet, background and shadow. Candidate arms rasterized from actual player_arm.png via the shared component renderer at native 2x scale. Head translation and facing were measured independently from the capture.
measurement.score: Higher is better: adding an arm pixel scores+1 on a reference skin pixel and-1 on background, counting overlap once. Unchanged body pixels excluded.
measurement.constraints: Source arm target families, opposing arms, rotation speeds and one-second turn sequence held fixed. Only fixed pose cadence and capture time origin varied.
measurement.selectedOriginBehavior: No added command delay or lead; initial elapsed0 uses neutral arm positions with captured smile.

limits: This is source-assisted pose reconstruction using actual avatar components, not verified pixel-perfect parity with the official client.
Silhouette fitting cannot uniquely identify arms fully occluded by the head or torso.
Reference palette, antialiasing, camera scale and shadow differ from the planner; these were excluded from fitting.
The 25 ms cadence is a fitted renderer choice, not evidence of an official game simulation tick.
Special instrument-specific dances and their sound cues are not reconstructed by this generic /dance sequence.

perFrameExperiment.method: Actual player components rasterized at native 2x scale in back arm, body, front arm order; front angle equals 360 minus back angle. Head translation and eye facing measured independently. RGB arm-region fit uses median skin-channel calibration from static head pixels. Dynamic programming limits arm motion to 1050 degrees/second, with a 0.05 score/degree motion cost and a 0.04 score/degree source-pose prior. The first four idle frames stay neutral.
perFrameExperiment.reason: The 218-frame recording lasts 7270 ms, shorter than the 12000 ms combined four-second facing and 600 ms foot repeat. Candidate four-second loops have discontinuous arm and body poses: 1130 ms to 5130 ms differs by 58 degrees and 2 logical pixels. The continuous 25 ms source-rules sampler remains active.
